papers.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
papers.authors: Nada Khogeer; Jerison Parra; Caroline Desgranges; Hugo Ribeiro
papers.abstract: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.

papers.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
papers.authors: Yu-Ning Zhang; Aleksandr S. Mokeev; Maximilian Rimbach-Russ; David P. DiVincenzo; Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski
papers.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
papers.authors: Ghansham Chandel; Siddhartha Das
papers.abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

papers.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
papers.authors: Josep Cabedo; Claudio Iacovelli; Leticia Tarruell; Alessio Celi
papers.abstract: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.

papers.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
papers.authors: Nathan McLane; Richard C. Remsing; Leah G. Dodson
papers.abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

papers.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
papers.authors: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares; Yevgeniy Kovchegov; Giorgio Torrieri
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Rényi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

papers.title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
papers.authors: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee; Harishankar Mishra; Asvija Balasubramanyam; S D Sudarsan; Gudapati Naresh Raghava
papers.abstract: Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of deterministic quantum search to NP problems while retaining the quadratic query advantage over classical exhaustive search.

papers.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
papers.authors: Sergey Shirobokov; Ben Jaderberg; Katerina Hristova; George Tsoukalas; Johannes Bausch; Eric Wieser; Francisco J. H. Heras; Nicholas C. Rubin; Guang Hao Low; Sébastien Racanière; Nenad Tomašev; Lei M. Zhang; James Watson; Tanuj Khattar; Aws Albarghouthi; Stavan Jain; Harun Khan; Leopoldo Sarra; Andrew W. Senior; Michael Broughton; Hussain Masoom; Sergio Boixo; Ryan Babbush; Swarat Chaudhuri; Pushmeet Kohli
papers.abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

papers.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
papers.authors: Yousef Mafi; K. G. S. H. Gunawardana; Kim Pöyhönen; Teemu Ojanen
papers.abstract: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
papers.authors: Yuan Deng; Zihan Hao; Honghao Lin; Qipeng Liu; Vahab Mirrokni; Jianan Shao; David P. Woodruff
papers.abstract: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+Ω(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

papers.title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Marco Rossignolo; Lorena C. Bianchet; Anurag Saha Roy; Shai Machnes
papers.abstract: Quantum technologies based on individually controlled atoms are among the most promising platforms for scalable quantum computing, owing to their favorable coherence properties and controllability. Nonetheless, achieving reliable and high-fidelity gate operations remains challenging due to the sensitivity of these systems to noise and hardware imperfections. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive software toolset designed to model atomic quantum systems with high precision and simulate qubit gate dynamics. By integrating quantum optimal control and benchmarking techniques with automatic differentiation for efficient and accurate gradient-based optimization, the toolset enables significant improvements in gate performance. We demonstrate its capabilities through detailed case studies involving both neutral atoms and trapped ions, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing quantum gate fidelities, and providing valuable insights for experimental implementation.

papers.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
papers.authors: David Turturean
papers.abstract: Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that every bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. They showed that the conjecture implies that the acceptance probability of every quantum algorithm making $T$ queries can be approximated on most inputs by a classical algorithm making $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ queries. We prove their conjecture: every function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ of degree at most $d\ge1$ has a variable of influence at least $c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^{6}$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. In the original formulation, for polynomials of degree at most $d$ with values in $[0,1]$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ and variance at least $\varepsilon$, this gives a variable of influence at least $(\varepsilon/d)^{7}$. The proof is elementary, with steps inspired by works of others. Thus, as Aaronson and Ambainis anticipated, superpolynomial quantum speedups in the query model require structure, such as a promise on the inputs.

papers.title: Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
papers.authors: Vittorio Pagni; Peter K. Schuhmacher; Michael Felderer; Michael Epping; Kevin Lively
papers.abstract: Efficient encoding of data into quantum states remains a fundamental bottleneck in many quantum computing protocols, which would otherwise offer advantages over their classical counterparts. Here, we introduce deterministic and scalable amplitude-encoding methods with low two-qubit gate costs and tunable trade-offs between circuit depth and encoding fidelity. Our approaches require no amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurement and are capable of encoding arbitrary complex data or queryable functions by using tensor-networks to go beyond what can be held in classical memory. Our principle contributions are two complementary algorithms for simplifying fully controlled multiplexer circuits to one- and two-qubit gates. In the first, we formally map the elimination of redundant gate controls to a Boolean logic minimization problem, while in the second we utilize a single ancilla qubit to map the multi-controlled rotation gates to a sequence of one- and two-qubit operations via the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of the gate angles. We benchmark these methods across a broad range of function classes, characterizing their total depth in an all-to-all connectivity graph against system size and target fidelity. Hybridizing our methods gives up to orders of magnitude improvement in circuit depth at equivalent state fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in the Qiskit package. We furthermore demonstrate our method on IQM hardware with a square lattice connectivity, finding excellent fidelity, even with minimal noise mitigation. By significantly reducing gate depth for encoding, this work enables the experimental execution of applications on current and near-term hardware which would otherwise be reduced to noise before the first calculation step, shortening the time horizon to robust quantum utility.

papers.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
papers.authors: Joohyung Song; James I. Kwon; Edo Waks; Saikat Guha; Chaohan Cui
papers.abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

papers.title: Witnessing Polarization Entanglement of Annihilation Photons via Compton Scattering
papers.authors: Tobias C. Sutter; Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
papers.abstract: Experimentally certifying polarization entanglement in annihilation photons is challenging because polarizers are unavailable in the high-energy regime and one needs to rely on Compton polarimetry. Previously proposed schemes designed for this task are either experimentally unfeasible or require a specific source state model. We address these issues by reformulating Compton scattering as a continuous-outcome quantum instrument, thereby enabling the prediction of the scattering angles and the post-scattering polarization state. Our framework allows connecting Compton polarimetry with entanglement witnesses by deriving experimentally accessible lower bounds on Bell state fidelities for arbitrary initial two-photon polarization states. We discuss how this witness can be extracted from coarse-grained coincidence measurements with detectors of almost any angular resolution. The presented scheme does not require knowledge of angle-independent empirical factors like detector efficiencies and source activity. Thus, our results provide a feasible route towards experimental entanglement certification in para-positronium decay with current technology.

papers.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
papers.authors: Usman Khan; Daniel Lopez; Venkat Aneesh Padmasola; Nirmal Dangi; Santosh Kumar; Yuping Huang
papers.abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

papers.title: An Adaptive Quantum Search Framework under Unknown Solution-density: Minimizing Expected Queries to the First Solution
papers.authors: Wiwat Asawalertsak; Rajchawit Sarochawikasit
papers.abstract: Grover's algorithm provides a mathematically optimal quadratic speedup for unstructured search, yet its standard formulation relies on a critical prerequisite: prior knowledge of the target solution count to determine the number of algorithm iterations. Although numerous strategies have been developed to identify or bypass this parameter, comparing them directly is nontrivial. This study investigates and computationally optimizes 3 prominent frameworks: Boyer-Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp, Fixed-Point search, and Density Estimation Methods. Density-specific benchmarks select the best tested method and configuration to minimize expected first-solution queries under 2 initialization-cost conventions. To translate these theoretical benchmarks into practical utility, a hybrid quantum-classical adaptive framework integrating Hill-climbing-assisted Grover Adaptive Search with state-space density estimation modeled via the Wang-Landau algorithm is proposed as a potential use-case. This implementation operates directly on the optimized query methods established earlier. Analytical models support the approach; ideal simulations show 18.8%-63.4% lower mean accumulated query costs than the tested randomized and fixed-point baselines.

papers.title: Spin to Orbital Angular Momentum Conversion in the Neutron Nucleus Weak Interaction
papers.authors: Niels Geerits; Stephan Sponar; Hartmut Lemmel; Andrea Piovano; Kyle Steffen; William Michael Snow
papers.abstract: The neutron nucleus weak interaction generates a small parity non conserving rotation of the neutron spin as the neutron moves through matter. This parity-odd neutron rotary power can reach up to 2.2e-3 rad * cm-1 for slow neutrons in 139La, which possesses a p-wave resonance at 0.7 eV where the parity-odd asymmetry is greatly amplified. This spin rotation must conserve total angular momentum. Here we show that this conservation occurs through neutron orbital angular momentum generation. We experimentally demonstrate that a neutron prepared initially in a longitudinal spin-orbit state experiences no change in total angular momentum.

papers.title: Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology
papers.authors: Rishith Reddy; Ashutosh Dubey; Partha Sarathi; Ankur Das
papers.abstract: In this work, we try to understand the question of how to address the survival of band topology in the presence of dephasing. We investigate this question in the Kane-Mele $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological insulator. To determine the stability of the topological invariant we construct a single particle Hamiltonian that also provides identical correlation at the single particle level. The phase transition from topological to trivial is determined by the gap closing of this correlation Hamiltonian. This gap closing is related to purity gap. As a diagnostics we calculated the invariant directly and as a complementary diagnostic, coherent two-terminal transport through the auxiliary correlation Hamiltonian exhibits quantized conductance in the nontrivial region. This does not establish physical conductance under dephasing. Our results identify a predictive local criterion for the survival of single-particle topological structure under a specified noise channel.

papers.title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
papers.authors: Mateusz Meller; Joseph C. R. Thacker; Thomas W. Keal; Vendel Szeremi
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.

papers.title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
papers.authors: A. K. Mandal; F. Zhang; J. H. Mikkelsen; M. Shen
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.

papers.title: Slices for normal forms in quantum information and a Riccati-type equation
papers.authors: Ranee Brylinski; Jean-Luc Brylinski
papers.abstract: It is known that the normal space to an orbit of a compact group linear action meets each orbit. We show that this yields known normal forms for quantum states. We compute the gradient flow converging to the normal form and find it gives a Riccati type matrix-valued ODE.

papers.title: Efficient One-Shot Simulation of Network Instruments and Multi-party Purity Distillation
papers.authors: Igor Bernard; Arun Padakandla
papers.abstract: We undertake an information theoretic study of instrument compression problems (ICPs) in {multiple network} configurations, wherein the goal is to design and analyze protocols that simulate specific quantum classical (QC) correlation amidst distributed parties - some holding components of the quantum state and the rest holding classical registers - with minimum communication. We present a \textit{unified framework} of protocols based on likelihood instruments whose analysis yields new inner bounds in the one-shot and asymptotic regimes for the different network configurations we study. Our framework comprises of a common template for designing the instrument simulation protocol and analyzing its information theoretic performance. We also address a related problem of multi-party purity distillation wherein three distributed parties have to distil pure states efficiently via local operations and minimal communication. In regards to the tools, in addition to one-shot purity concentration protocol of \cite{202203arXiv_ChaPadSen} and one-shot quantum simultaneous decoder of Sen \cite{202102SAD_Sen}, we leverage Sen's fully smooth multi-partite covering \cite{202504arXiv_Sen} for all of our covering bounds.

papers.title: Quantum subsets discrimination and key sifting with success probability one
papers.authors: D. A. Kronberg
papers.abstract: Non-distinguishability of non-orthogonal quantum states is the essential feature of quantum mechanics. In particular, one cannot deterministically orthogonalize the set of quantum states, while probabilistic orthogonalization is possible, including unambiguous state discrimination and discrimination between the subsets. Here, we propose a method for error-free subsets discrimination with significantly increased success probability, which may reach one even for non-orthogonal and linearly dependent input states. This method may be applied in quantum cryptography: An alternative basis reconciliation procedure is described, which may provide unit sifting probability even for a large number of bases and for non-orthogonal states within each basis.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
papers.authors: Gregory C. Levine; Goncalo C. Oliveira
papers.abstract: Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $ρ$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log ρ$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.

papers.title: Magic Can Superactivate Quantum Capacity
papers.authors: Chunhe Xiong; Sunho Kim; Shunlong Luo; Lin Zhang; Shao-Ming Fei; Junde Wu
papers.abstract: Environmental magic can enable two channels with zero quantum capacity to transmit quantum information jointly. We establish this superactivation within a family of discrete quantum convolution channels with fixed Clifford interactions. For the couplings considered, stabilizer-mixture environments induce entanglement-breaking channels. We construct a mixed magic environment whose induced channel has positive private capacity and a Choi state with positive partial transpose, hence zero quantum capacity. A half-erasure auxiliary activates this channel through the Smith--Yard mechanism. Finite-block encoding and decoding over a self-complementary convolution auxiliary then realize a higher-dimensional erasure channel that still permits activation. We also bound the activated capacity by the modified relative entropy of magic of the main environment. Replacing either environment of the convolution pair by any stabilizer mixture makes the joint quantum capacity vanish, identifying environmental magic as a necessary resource on both sides for this realization.

papers.title: Scanning Probe Control, Quantum Dynamics, and Dispersive Readout of Suspended Carbon Nanotube Resonators
papers.authors: Cristian Staii
papers.abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer promising opportunities for quantum nanomechanics owing to their small effective mass, strong electrostatic tunability, and mechanical nonlinearity. We develop a unified theoretical framework for coherent control and readout of a suspended CNT driven by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip and capacitively coupled to a Cooper-pair box (CPB). We first derive the linear and nonlinear Duffing response of the CNT and quantify the effects of AFM force gradients, tip-position fluctuations, and voltage noise on mechanical stability, dephasing, and heating. These results establish operating conditions for coherent actuation with limited backaction. We then quantize the Duffing oscillator, derive its Kerr anharmonicity, and identify the requirements for selective control of individual vibrational transitions. Estimates of thermal occupation and active cooling illustrate the constraints for CNT modes spanning frequencies from 54 MHz to 5.37 GHz. Finally, we derive the CNT--CPB interaction and its dispersive limit, showing how phonon number and parity can be mapped onto the CPB through Ramsey interferometry and detected using quantum-capacitance readout. The resulting framework identifies the conditions under which localized AFM actuation, nonlinear quantum dynamics, and superconducting state-resolved detection can operate within a single CNT device.

papers.title: BQP-Complete Susceptibilities Observable at Ballistic Times in Local Quantum Dynamics
papers.authors: Yuting Lyu
papers.abstract: Local response measurements track how perturbations spread in quantum simulators and nonequilibrium many-body systems. Locality bounds constrain the propagation speed, but do not determine whether the response can distinguish computational outcomes at fixed measurement precision as the distance increases. Here we construct time-independent dynamics with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions in which a fixed single-site detector responds to a remote bond phase after a time proportional to their separation. The susceptibility has a positive lower bound independent of distance. With product-state preparations, estimating this susceptibility to constant additive accuracy is complete for bounded-error quantum polynomial time (BQP), with a decision gap independent of distance. Two source-phase settings give the susceptibility with a distance-independent shot count at fixed accuracy and confidence. Inverse-polynomially weak local couplings between the computational register and the chain carrying the excitation preserve the gap. The leading correction vanishes when exchanging the two internal states of the excitation reverses the interaction. Varying the source and observation time makes all bond phases locally identifiable near the zero-phase reference setting. We also prove a conditional quantum advantage for distribution-free response prediction.

papers.title: Relativistic analogue of the Kramers-Henneberger transformation and pair creation
papers.authors: Johannes Marschall; Christian Kohlfürst; Naser Ahmadiniaz; Ralf Schützhold
papers.abstract: In analogy to the Kramers-Henneberger transformation in non-relativistic quantum mechanics, we propose and investigate a spinor transformation for the Dirac equation which allows us to transform space-time dependent vector potentials $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}$_x away. In the mass-less case, we exactly arrive at the free Dirac equation, while for massive Dirac fields, the transformation results in a non-trivial mass matrix containing space-time dependent phases. Special emphasis is placed on the phenomenon of fermion pair creation in the external field $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}_x$ where the spinor transformation allows us to conceptually disentangle the different contributions to pair creation. It can also be used to reformulate the WKB approach and the Riccati equation (which can be advantageous in certain cases) and to obtain additional insight into the mechanism of dynamically assisted pair creation.

papers.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
papers.authors: Yuri Ogami; Hiroyasu Tajima
papers.abstract: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can induce a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. Here, we answer this question systematically. We first construct an explicit model and prove that coupling to an environment can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system, even without such resource supply. We consider Lindblad master equations with (i) time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, (ii) time-translation covariance, and (iii) detailed balance---conditions that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. Our model satisfies these conditions, and the activation occurs in a stationary state of both the isolated and open systems. We give several implementations of this dynamics with a zero-temperature Gibbs environment, a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, and only short-range Hamiltonians, one of which exactly reproduces the time-crystalline periodicity. We then prove a no-go theorem: under (i)--(iii), activation can arise only from an environment-induced Hamiltonian term, not from dissipation. Our results show that time crystals can be activated in open systems without external resource supply and identify the physical requirements on the system and environment for this activation through our general no-go theorem.

papers.title: Twisted Compactification, Quotient Quantum Codes and Logical Gates
papers.authors: Po-Shen Hsin
papers.abstract: Many quantum codes, including balanced-product, bivariate-bicycle and genon codes and the five-qubit code, are quotient codes: a larger code folded onto itself by identifying each check with its image under a deck transformation composed with a symmetry. We show that this is the lattice form of twisted compactification, in which a theory on $X\times F$ carries a symmetry background along $F$, and we use the correspondence in both directions. For monomial quotients of Pauli stabilizer codes, a transfer theorem gives the logical qudits, logical operators and distance bounds from those of the parent, with a Tate cohomology group counting the logical operators that are new. For higher-form and cup-product symmetries the twist is an entangling diagonal circuit; when a finite cover trivializes the background, the code is a dressed quotient, so abelian Pauli codes give non-abelian topological order such as $D(D_4)$. The dressings have Clifford level at most one less than the degree of the twist, and for cubic twists the code dimension is a count of solutions of quadratic equations in cup products, which certifies that the code is not a Pauli stabilizer code when it is not a power of two; on tori and slabs the distance is linear in the size. Twists also create logical gates: three toric codes on $S^3$ have no logical qubits, but on $\mathbb{RP}^3$ the same circuit is a logical $CCZ$. A quarter-turn twist of the 3D fermionic toric code gives codes of linear distance, from $[[768,2,9]]$ up, whose $p+ip$ pump is an explicit finite-time quasi-local evolution that preserves the code space exactly; using the spin-topological response formula of Barkeshli, Hsin and Kobayashi, we identify its logical action as $T$ up to Clifford factors. Finally, twisting abelian gauge theories reach only the quantum doubles $D(G)$ with $[G,G]$ central.

papers.title: Resonance-engineered single-photon routing in an asymmetric Jaynes-Cummings cavity-waveguide system
papers.authors: Adam Sulieman Ibrahim Abdalla
papers.abstract: We investigate single-photon scattering and routing in an asymmetric cavity-waveguide quantum electrodynamics system consisting of a Jaynes-Cummings cavity-emitter subsystem coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides. Using a real-space scattering approach, we derive an exact three-channel scattering matrix and analytical expressions for the channel-resolved scattering amplitudes. The scattering response is governed by the interplay of asymmetric cavity-waveguide coupling, atom-cavity detuning, coherent preparation of a single-photon superposition across multiple input channels, and intrinsic dissipation. Coupling asymmetry controls the relative weights of the cavity-mediated scattering pathways, whereas atom-cavity detuning modifies their spectral response. Coherent multichannel input states provide an additional phase-sensitive control of the output probabilities through interference. In particular, we identify an analytical condition, $J_2=2J_1$ and $α_1=-α_2$, under which the probability in the second output channel becomes independent of photon energy; for an equal-weight normalized input, this probability is 1/2. We further show how cavity and atomic dissipation reduce the probability remaining in the guided channels. These results provide a framework for resonance-engineered single-photon routing in asymmetric Jaynes-Cummings cavity-waveguide systems.

papers.title: Direct-decision quantum sensing for classifying transient NMR signals
papers.authors: Juha Leppäkangas; Michael Marthaler
papers.abstract: Task-oriented quantum sensing aims to extract decision-relevant information directly, without first reconstructing the full signal. We study this approach for mixture-threshold classification of transient NMR-like signals generated from molecular spin Hamiltonians, motivated by small-volume molecular sensing. Using analytical models and numerical simulations, we compare classical coil readout followed by matched-filter classification with quantum computational sensing (QCS), in which trainable controls interleaved with signal-driven sensor-qubit evolution map the transient directly to a decision score. We consider both the sensor-ensemble limit and strict single-sensor single-shot readout. Increasing QCS control depth can improve robustness and class-dependent output contrast. Ensemble accuracy can rise rapidly for some waveform pairs, whereas single-shot correctness improves more gradually because one projective outcome must distinguish the classes. Repeated acquisitions improve both routes by averaging independent fluctuations, while disorder-aware training mitigates quasistatic inhomogeneity in the modeled sensor ensemble. QCS can outperform inductive readout under the modeled conditions, for example when coil transfer is weak or receiver noise limits coil performance. However, the simulated QCS protocols at lower effective sensor coupling require long sensing intervals, whereas short-time protocols require a much stronger effective drive at the sensor. Practical advantage therefore depends on jointly attainable source-signal strength, signal-to-sensor transfer, qubit coherence, and readout resources.

papers.title: Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
papers.authors: Llorenç Escolà-Farràs; Florian Speelman
papers.abstract: The BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement (MoE) game has numerous applications in quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, position verification, and unclonable encryption. In this short note, we improve the error threshold for parallel repetition with identical answer strings from the approximately $3.7\%$ certified by the original bound to the sharp threshold $(1-1/\sqrt2)/2\approx14.64\%$. When the players need not give identical answers, we also obtain exponential decay whenever the sum of their error tolerances is below this threshold. These bounds strengthen existing security reductions to the BB84 MoE game, improving security bounds and certified noise tolerances for cryptographic protocols.

papers.title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
papers.authors: Georgios E. Pavlou; Ioannis Kiorpelidis; Georgios K. Simopoulos; Manas Kulkarni; Konstantinos G. Makris
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.

papers.title: Symmetry-Resolved Criticality in Dissipative Quantum Phase Transitions
papers.authors: Xingli Li; Yan Li; Jinghui Pi; Wenlin Li; Shuai Geng; Lin Shang; Jiasen Jin; Yangqian Yan
papers.abstract: Symmetry breaking in mixed quantum states exhibits a rich strong-to-weak hierarchy, yet the use of symmetry as an operational probe of dissipative criticality remains largely unexplored. In this work, we develop a symmetry-based framework that connects semiclassical phase space, trajectory-level dynamics, and ensemble responses, and demonstrate it in the two-dimensional dissipative XYZ model. We show that symmetry breaking manifests semiclassically as a bifurcation of the Husimi-Q distribution and dynamically as a sharp change in a trajectory-level symmetry residual. At the ensemble level, the weak-symmetry sensitivity to a perturbed symmetry operator exhibits pronounced finite-size scaling, yielding an estimate of the dissipative critical point. Finally, we propose a trajectory-based quantum-circuit algorithm in which mid-circuit measurements condition quantum jumps and allow the proposed indicators to be extracted from circuit observables. Our work provides a symmetry-centered route to diagnosing dissipative phase transitions and critical scaling in open quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
papers.authors: Sarah Ashby; David Bostanjyan; Mikayel Khanbekyan
papers.abstract: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.

papers.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
papers.authors: Vimal Sreekanth; Chandrima B. Pushpan; Amit Kumar Pal
papers.abstract: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

papers.title: Quantum-induced latent symmetries
papers.authors: Jonas Himmel; Malte Röntgen; Tilman Gühlstorf; Matthias Heinrich; Max Ehrhardt; Alexander Szameit; Tom A. W. Wolterink
papers.abstract: We study the interplay of latent symmetries and multiparticle quantum states upon the introduction of additional particles. We show how physical symmetries in multimode quantum systems give rise to symmetries in the multiparticle state space of indistinguishable fermions and bosons. Latent symmetries, hidden symmetries that are exclusively visible in the eigenspectral domain, offer new ways to engineer the functionality of multimode quantum systems. In this vein, we present multiboson state generation as an application of latent symmetries to the multiparticle domain. Finally, we demonstrate that even in systems that are entirely devoid of symmetry, latent symmetries can be induced in the multiparticle state space, as a result of quantum indistinguishability.

papers.title: Flexible Control of Temporal Reflection and Refraction via Joint Parameter Modulation
papers.authors: Liu-Shan Zhang; Cheng-Qi Wu; Dong Yan; Hong Yang; Han-Xiao Zhang; Chu-Hui Fan
papers.abstract: Achieving the flexible control of wave propagation is a central goal in the design of optical devices. In this work, our analytical results and numerical simulations show that in both the two-legged model and SSH model, joint modulation of coupling strengths and phases enables independent control of the probability partition and the propagation opening angles in the space-time map. We hope these results could provide a theoretical foundation for the design of programmable time-modulated optical devices.

papers.title: Motion-Induced Polaron Resonance beyond the Orthogonality Catastrophe
papers.authors: Jia Wang; Xia-Ji Liu; Hui Hu
papers.abstract: We investigate the spectroscopic response of a repulsively interacting, infinitely heavy impurity moving at constant velocity $v$ through a one-dimensional ideal Fermi gas. Using an exact functional-determinant approach, we calculate the Ramsey response and spectral function, fully accounting for many-body particle-hole excitations. We uncover a strongly nonmonotonic dependence on impurity velocity: decoherence is enhanced around the Fermi velocity, whereas sufficiently rapid motion restores a narrow, long-lived polaron resonance. A long-time wave-packet analysis yields analytical expressions for the polaron energy and decay rate over the full velocity range and quantitatively captures the numerical results. At high velocity, the polaron energy approaches the mean-field value, the decay rate vanishes as $1/v$, and the spectral weight approaches unity. Thus, rapid prescribed motion provides a dynamical route to suppressing the orthogonality catastrophe and restoring polaron coherence even for an infinitely heavy impurity, where recoil is entirely absent.

papers.title: Enhanced-sensitivity optical sensing of magnetic fields using postselected amplification and continuous-wave power recycling
papers.authors: Yazhi Niu; Jialin Li; Lupei Qin; Xin-Qi Li
papers.abstract: Given the importance of precision weak magnetic field measurement, and noting that postselected amplification has not yet been well applied in this area, in this work we propose to combine the technique of postselected amplification with continuous-wave power recycling for enhanced-sensitivity optical sensing of weak magnetic fields. Based on rigorous derivations, we obtain compact expressions for the total postselection probability and the signal-to-noise ratio. We also analyze the effects originating from various non-ideal factors. In contrast to pulse recycling, continuous-wave recycling has lower control requirements and is more experimentally feasible.

papers.title: Tomography of approximately Gaussian mixed states
papers.authors: S. Nibedita Swain; Timothy C. Ralph; Jens Eisert; Nathan Walk
papers.abstract: Moment-based tomography efficiently reconstructs Gaussian states, but stochastic phase noise generally produces mixed, non-Gaussian outputs. For approximately Gaussian outputs, we formulate reconstruction as a problem in quantum learning theory under model misspecification. Our trace-distance guarantee separates the intrinsic Gaussian approximation error from statistical errors in estimating the first moments and covariance matrix. Using recent Gaussian trace-distance bounds, we obtain linear dependence of the statistical contribution on moment errors when the covariance inverses remain bounded, improving on the square-root dependence on covariance error in earlier guarantees. A Fock-space truncation procedure provides certified, convergent lower and upper bounds on the intrinsic error. Under an explicit sub-Gaussian condition on the heterodyne outcomes, the sufficient sample count scales inversely with the square of the allowed statistical error remaining after accounting for the approximation error. We verify the statistical condition for stochastic phase rotations and heralded unitary-averaged states with bounded input squeezing. We apply the framework to probabilistic unitary averaging for phase noise reduction, quantifying reconstruction error and accounting for heralding overhead in the total number of estimation attempts.

papers.title: Critical properties of EPR steering
papers.authors: Yu-Xuan Zhang; Jing-Ling Chen
papers.abstract: Every PVM-critical entangled two-qubit state becomes steerable with two copies. We prove this for the full critical boundary and for two different critical inputs. The joint measurements can have arbitrarily little entanglement, while all conditional states on Bob's two systems remain separable. Criticality is exactly the point where this measurement-entanglement threshold vanishes. The number of measurements has a separate critical behavior: every fixed setting bound leaves an unsteerable neighborhood of the critical input. Moreover, for any such bound, there are critical states that remain unsteerable under every tensor power, although unrestricted measurements activate them with two copies. These results identify different roles for measurement entanglement, measurement number, and collective access in revealing steering. We also construct fixed-dimensional states whose steering activates on two copies while Bell locality persists through any prescribed finite copy range. In increasing dimension, the two-copy steering violation is unbounded, giving an affirmative solution to the amplification question of Hsieh, Liang, and Lee.

papers.title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
papers.authors: Andrew Powell
papers.abstract: The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{Iα}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_Γ=\exp(IqΦ_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_Γ= (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.

papers.title: Correlation-Enhanced Quantum Reservoir Processing for Two-Qutrit Steering: From Generalization to Discovery
papers.authors: Pu Wang; Zhongyan Li; Huixian Meng; Yutao Xin. Ziqi Zhi; Zhihua Guo; Huaixin Cao
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir processing (QRP) has been applied to entanglement quantification, yet its potential for generalizable steering detection and the discovery of high-dimensional quantum correlations remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce correlation-enhanced QRP (CEQRP), extending QRP to two-qutrit systems with two-body spin-correlation readouts. Some CEQRP-based classifiers substantially improve cross-family generalization, with logistic regression trained on full-information CEQRP features achieving approximately $96\%$ accuracy on unseen Werner states and over $97\%$ accuracy on unseen isotropic states at both \(m=4\) and \(m=5\). Independently, we establish two interconnected steering criteria for mixed two-qutrit states: a necessary-and-sufficient all-versus-nothing criterion for states admitting three linearly independent pure conditional states, and an asymptotic sufficient criterion, with the two criteria linked through invertible local filtering. These criteria provide rigorously certified steerable samples for training-set augmentation. Combining CEQRP-based classification with these theory-certified samples enables the discovery of new Alice-to-Bob steerable partially entangled states, including states at \(p=0.45\) whose steerability is independently confirmed by semidefinite programming (SDP) using seven projective measurement settings. The trained classifiers further guide finite-setting searches for steering boundaries. Our results establish a pathway from generalizable classification to the discovery of high-dimensional quantum steering.

papers.title: Evaluation of Quantum Machine Learning Models for Network Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Swathi Chandrasekhar; Shiva Raj Pokhrel
papers.abstract: The proliferation of Internet-connected devices has intensified the risk of large-scale network intrusions, necessitating more advanced detection methodologies for the post quantum era. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, a com- prehensive investigation of quantum machine learning (QML) for anomaly detection on the BoT-IoT dataset, a widely adopted benchmark for IoT security. Leveraging feature-engineered rep- resentations, we implement and evaluate four representative quantum classifiers: Quantum Support Vector Classification (QSVC), Quantum Neural Networks (QNN), and Variational Quantum Classifiers (VQC).

papers.title: Reachability Constraints and Monotones for Quantum-State Texture
papers.authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon; Pablo Vielman; Miguel Gonzalez
papers.abstract: How a quantum resource can be quantified depends on which operations are free. Yet two proposed quantifiers of quantum state texture can increase under free operations: the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information relative to the unique textureless state and the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance from that state. We show reachability from every state orthogonal to the textureless state, whether pure or mixed: each can be freely transformed into any other state. Therefore, every texture monotone must assign the same maximal value to all such states, a requirement that neither candidate satisfies. We then construct valid texture monotones by adding the population outside the textureless state to the skew information and by maximizing the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance over free operations. We prove faithfulness, convexity, and invariance under textureless ancillas, characterize additivity properties and strong monotonicity, satisfied only in the Wigner-Yanase case, and derive tight bounds for both monotones at fixed overlap with the textureless state and characterize all saturating states. Together, these results show how allowed state transformations impose operational constraints on the quantification of quantum state texture.

papers.title: Exploring Variational Regularization of Krylov Subspaces
papers.authors: Alexandre Perrin; Jérémie Messud; Sébastien Burdin; Matthieu Saubanère
papers.abstract: Krylov subspace methods efficiently approximate extremal eigenstates and eigenvalues of many-body Hamiltonians, but non-orthogonal bases can suffer from ill-conditioning. This challenge is amplified in quantum computing, where direct state access and thus straightforward orthogonalization are unavailable. We investigate a variational Krylov-like framework that iteratively optimizes a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies. Analyzed against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model, ansatz expressivity strongly influences the performance: Hamiltonian-inspired ansätze preserve Krylov-like convergence while improving the conditioning, whereas shallow ansätze remain stable but miss low-energy directions.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Practical QKD Post-Processing Algorithms Using a GUI-Based Simulation Framework
papers.authors: Ushnik Nath; Neha Sharma; Ramniwas Meena; Neel Kanth Kundu
papers.abstract: Recent experimental demonstrations of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) have attracted significant attention for their ability to establish information-theoretically secure encryption keys for next-generation communication systems. As practical deployment accelerates, the realization of compact, scalable, and high-throughput discrete-variable (DV) QKD systems has become increasingly important. While advances in photonic integration are enabling low-size, low-weight, and low-power QKD hardware, the security and performance of these systems rely heavily on efficient post-processing techniques to generate identical, secure keys. This tutorial presents a comprehensive algorithm-level review of practical post-processing techniques for DV-QKD, with particular emphasis on information reconciliation methods based on Cascade, Winnow, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and polar codes. We also analyze the theoretical asymptotic and finite-size secret key rates (SKRs) of DV-QKD and benchmark these bounds against the practical SKRs achieved using actual post-processing algorithms. Furthermore, we present a server-client model to implement the entire QKD post-processing pipeline. The performance is evaluated in terms of QBER and SKR across various system parameters, considering the complete post-processing pipeline, including sifting, information reconciliation, privacy amplification, and authentication. This tutorial also presents a graphical user interface (GUI) for the QKD post-processing methods, enabling researchers, industry practitioners, and academic users to visualize and analyze the impact of different post-processing techniques and system parameters, such as QBER, on the SKR performance of DV-QKD systems.

papers.title: Single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain: beyond independent radiation
papers.authors: Juliette Jiménez-Jaimes; Étienne Brion
papers.abstract: We study single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain, comparing a full microscopic model with an independent-radiation approximation. We show that nearly equal transmission probabilities can coexist with substantially different transmitted temporal modes, even after adjusting their relative delay. For a reference chain, a decomposition into collective atomic resonances relates this discrepancy mainly to spectral-phase changes caused by the omitted interatomic couplings. Parameter scans delimit this phase-dominated regime, and controlled comparisons separate the effects of coherent exchange and collective decay.

papers.title: Interaction-enabled charging and thermal crossover of the spin-work deficit in a Hubbard double quantum dot
papers.authors: Khalil Loukhssami; Cheng Shang; Morad El Baz; Khadija El Hawary
papers.abstract: We study how conservation of total spin affects the extractable work of an interacting Hubbard double quantum dot charged in the presence of unresolved quasistatic detuning fluctuations. The full fermionic Fock space is used to model preparation through electronic reservoirs, whereas the additional work deficit associated with spin conservation arises entirely from the singlet and triplet states at half filling. At zero detuning, modulation of the symmetric tunnel barrier couples two singlets of even parity. The corresponding transition matrix element vanishes when U = V . An exact formula for the additional work deficit follows from passive spectral rearrangement under two extraction constraints: conservation of particle number alone and conservation of both particle number and total spin. At low temperature, an expansion in the detuning response gives a leading estimate of the noise amplitude at which this deficit first appears. Increasing the preparation temperature changes the triplet population and produces a crossover at s2 = q, where the additional spin constraint becomes nonbinding for the averaged state, even though both ergotropies may continue to decrease. We obtain a semi-analytic expression for this crossover by separating the thermal Gibbs weights from the singlet dynamics under a fixed charging pulse. Averaging over symmetric detuning disorder also restores parity in the density matrix and allows singlet eigenvalues of different parity to exchange order, changing the branch that determines the thermal boundary. The work values are optimal over specified classes of unitary operations and do not establish the yield of a finite discharge protocol.

papers.title: Parametric $\mathrm{CZ}$ Gates in a Tunable Tripod Architecture with Fixed-Frequency Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: Chanpyo Kim; Hansol Kim; Jeongsoo Kang; Younghun Kwon
papers.abstract: Efficient implementation of the operations required for quantum error correction in superconducting quantum computers requires high gate fidelity, adequate qubit connectivity, and selective control of interactions. Sharing a single coupler among multiple qubits can improve connectivity, but also requires accounting for its effects on qubits outside the target pair. In this work, we numerically investigate the feasibility of implementing parametric-resonance $\mathrm{CZ}$ gates in a tunable tripod structure consisting of three fixed-frequency transmon qubits connected to a single tunable coupler. We modulate the external flux applied to the coupler and optimize the pulse parameters for each qubit pair to construct $\mathrm{CZ}_{01}$, $\mathrm{CZ}_{02}$, and $\mathrm{CZ}_{12}$ gates. We calculate the time evolution of a Hamiltonian that includes three energy levels for each circuit element and evaluate gate fidelity and leakage after virtual Z correction. The fidelities obtained for the target-pair computational blocks, whose input and output basis states have both the coupler and spectator qubit in their ground states, are 0.9943, 0.9834, and 0.9907, respectively. We also find that population preservation at the end of the gate depends on the initial state of the spectator qubit. These results demonstrate the possibility of constructing $\mathrm{CZ}$ operations for each qubit pair through flux modulation of a shared coupler while maintaining fixed data-qubit frequencies. They also highlight the need to evaluate performance and optimize control over the full computational space, including the spectator qubit.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge and exact solution of the $\pm J$ Edwards-Anderson model in a transverse field
papers.authors: Mikhail Vasin
papers.abstract: Using the Majorana representation of spin-1/2 operators, we study the $\pm J$ Edwards--Anderson model in a transverse field at $T=0$. We show that, in this representation, the quantity describing the coupling between neighboring spins commutes with the Hamiltonian and, unlike in the Kitaev model, is not subject to any Gauss law. The resulting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge freedom allows the disorder in the signs of the exchange integrals to be eliminated by an exact gauge transformation, so that the spectrum of the system coincides with that of the model with uniform couplings. The resulting theory is quadratic in the Majorana fields. Computing the local Green's functions, we find that the Edwards--Anderson order parameter vanishes for $Δ>J\sqrt{Z}$ and equals $1/4$ for $Δ<J\sqrt{Z}$, which signals a second-order transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass ground state that is degenerate over spin configurations and replica symmetric at $T=0$.

papers.title: Quantum-Enhanced Classical Communications for DPMZM-based NG-PON2 Systems
papers.authors: Parvin Kumar; Sourav Banerjee; Neel Kanth Kundu; Umesh Sharma
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework for integrating quantum detection techniques into a Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DPMZM)-based Next Generation Passive Optical Network 2 (NG-PON2) communication system. We present a system model for the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system and characterize its signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), demonstrating its superiority over conventional MZM-based systems. We analyze the performance of various quantum modulation techniques, including binary phase-shift keying, quadrature phase-shift keying, and M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation. A comprehensive analytical framework is developed to evaluate the SNR, BER, and mutual information for both classical and quantum detection schemes within the DPMZM-based NG-PON2 quantum communication system. Our simulation results show that quantum detection significantly outperforms classical detection, and the DPMZM architecture further enhances the performance over the baseline MZM architecture by improving the effective modulation efficiency and receiver sensitivity.

papers.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
papers.authors: Davide Batic; Denys Dutykh
papers.abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

papers.title: Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
papers.authors: Tatsuya Yamanouchi; Naoto Shiraishi
papers.abstract: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios.
